subject: Critical Thinking
subcategory: Evidence & Truth: How We Know What's Real
title: Rationalism: Knowledge from Reason Alone
description: A 60-second lesson on Rationalism: Knowledge from Reason Alone.

hook.text: Descartes locked himself in a room with no experiments. Through pure reason alone, he tried to find certain knowledge.

buildup.text: Rationalism: the view that reason – not experience – is the primary source of knowledge.

discovery.text: 'Cogito, ergo sum' — I think, therefore I am. Descartes found one indubitable truth through reason alone.

twist.text: Mathematics is the rationalist's triumph: 2+2=4 needs no experiment.

climax.text: Modern philosophy combines both: empirical evidence for facts about the world, reason for logical & mathematical truths.

punchline.text: Some truths you see. Some truths you think. Both are real.

quiz.question: What did Descartes establish through pure reason?
options: That thinking proves his own existence (cogito ergo sum)

details.summary: Rationalism holds that some knowledge can be obtained through reason alone, independent of sensory experience. Mathematics and logic are the strongest cases for rationalist knowledge existing prior to any observation.
details.whyItMatters: Rationalism reminds us that not all knowledge is empirical. Logical deduction and mathematical proof reveal truths that no experiment could discover.
takeaways: Some truths can be known through pure reasoning
Descartes, Leibniz, and Spinoza were major rationalists
Mathematics is the strongest example of non-empirical knowledge

faq.question: What is the most famous argument for rationalism?
faq.answer: Descartes's 'I think, therefore I am.' By doubting everything, Descartes showed that the very act of doubting proved the existence of a thinker. This knowledge comes from pure reason, not observation.

faq.question: How do modern thinkers reconcile rationalism and empiricism?
faq.answer: Most accept that both contribute to knowledge. Mathematics and logic provide a priori truths, while natural science requires empirical evidence. The debate is about emphasis, not absolute exclusion of either approach.
